newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court hears security scandal case.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court hears security scandal case.

text.p: A Turkish court on Monday began the trial of 11 people, mostly junior police officers, over a security scandal that revealed ties between the state and organised crime, Anatolian news agency said.
"The trial of 11 suspects started today in Istanbul State Security Court," the state-run agency said.

The scandal erupted last November when a car crashed in western town of Susurluk killing a wanted gangaster, a top police officer and a former beauty queen. Government MP Sedat Bucak, who heads a pro-state Kurdish militia, was in the same car but survived.
The accident spurred a series of media reports that painted a picture of gangsters using state privileges and political connections to kill opponents, trade drugs and traffic in guns.
Interior Minister Mehmet Agar resigned after the media implicated him in the affair. He remains a government MP.
Anatolian said 10 suspects faced up to nine years in jail if found guilty under Article 313 of the penal code for forming an armed gang that threatened the security of the state.

The chief of a special police unit, Ibrahim Sahin, and the former bodyguards of MP Bucak, who has close ties to the current government, were among the 10. An 11th suspect could be jailed for up to four years for alleged membership in an armed gang.

In a separate case last week the driver whose truck hit the car became the only person convicted so far. He was fined the equivalent of $43 and made to pay $720 in damages to relatives of those who died in the crash.
Opposition efforts to probe leading political and police figures suspected of involvement in the scandal have so far gone nowhere.
